call_points.text: Total cumulative capex now close to ₹4,000 Cr, over and above the October 2024 programme.
Added capacity of 30 GVA, up to 40 GVA on product mix, roughly doubling the existing transformer factory.
Most contracts carry commodity price pass-through, but inflated freight cannot be passed on, per management.
Analysts pressed on weak non-HVDC domestic order inflow; management said base orders grew but gave no figure.
Royalty continues because technology comes from the parent; the company does no R&D spend of its own.
Mumbai city infeed of 1,000 MW on VSC technology commissioned, with converter stations at Aarey and Kudus.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: After the completion of scrutiny assessment for FY 2020-21, the Company had received a show cause notice under section 148A (procedure before issuance of notice u/s 148) for re-assessment under section 147 on March 29, 2025. The Company had responded to the said notice in April 2025 with full explanation highlighting that there is no escapement of income during the assessment proceedings. However, the Assessing Officer did not take the same into account and initiated the reassessment proceedings by passing the order u/s 148A(3) on June 30, 2025. In the said order, the Assessing Officer has proposed an adjustment to taxable income to the tune of Rs. 28,06,45,970 with corresponding tax impact of Rs. 9,39,41,860 including interest. As per the Income-tax law provisions, the proceedings u/s 148 of the Act should be carried out though automated allocation and under faceless assessment manner. Hence, the Company believes that the notice and the order issued by the Jurisdictional Assessing Officer u/s 148 of the Act are bad in law and are liable to be quashed. Notwithstanding the same, the Company had filed a revised return u/s 148 on August 25, 2025 (replica of the original return) as required under the provisions of the Act. Further, the Company has responded to the notice in the month of October, 2025, with all necessary supporting documents to justify that the expenses claimed by the Company were in order and are allowable under the provisions of the Act. The re-assessment proceedings are yet to be disposed off.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: The Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax
tax_litigation.status: The Company has received a notice under Section 143(2) read with Section 147 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 on June 22, 2026, seeking supporting documents and evidence in relation to the return of income filed. The Company is in the process of furnishing the requisite details and supporting evidence before the tax authorities within the prescribed timeline. The matter has been adjourned and is currently scheduled for hearing on July 14, 2026.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: This case was selected for scrutiny assessment for FY2021-22, pursuant to which the Assessing Officer (“AO”) referred the matter to the Transfer Pricing Officer (“TPO”) for carrying out the transfer pricing assessment. The transfer pricing assessment was concluded and the TPO proposed a transfer pricing adjustment aggregating to INR 113.2 crores on account of alleged low margins in the manufacturing segment, system integration segment and deemed interest on delayed receivables. The transfer pricing order was issued on January 23, 2025. Subsequently, the AO passed a draft assessment order under section 144C(1) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 on March 4, 2025, incorporating the proposed transfer pricing adjustments. In addition, the AO disallowed Group Management Fees amounting to INR 69.95 crores, without duly considering the submissions made by the Company. Aggrieved by the draft assessment order, the Company filed objections before the Dispute Resolution Panel (“DRP”) on April 2, 2025. The DRP issued its directions on December 26, 2025, largely confirming the adjustments proposed by the TPO. However, with respect to the Group Management Fees, while the DRP confirmed the disallowance made by the AO, it directed that the said fees should not be considered while computing the margins for the manufacturing segment and system integration segment. Pursuant to the directions of the DRP, the AO passed the final assessment order on January 21, 2026, wherein the Group Management Fees amounting to INR 699.5 million and interest on delayed receivables amounting to INR 16.4 million were disallowed. On account of these disallowances, the segmental margins improved and were within the range determined by the TPO. Consequently, the transfer pricing adjustment aggregating to INR 1,114.8 million was deleted, resulting in a reduced tax demand of INR 260.9 million as against the earlier demand of INR 435.8 million. The Company is of the view that no addition is warranted in respect of the disallowance of Group Management Fees and notional interest on delayed receivables. Accordingly, the Company has preferred an appeal before the Income-tax Appellate Tribunal (“ITAT”) on March 25, 2026 against the aforesaid additions.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: The Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax
tax_litigation.status: The Company has received a notice from the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) scheduling the hearing in the matter on August 19, 2026. The Company is in the process of preparing and filing the paper book and other supporting documents in accordance with the prescribed procedures and timelines.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Post de-merger, non-novated transactions were carried out with ABB India Limited ('ABB') in FY 2019-20 & FY 2020-21 and offshore sales by transfer of documents of title to the goods were transacted. The goods moved from a country (other than India) and where destined for Nepal / Bangladesh / Sri Lanka. While raising invoice on ABB we had charged GST. However, since these transactions were carried out entirely outside India, no GST should have been charged. Accordingly, The Company had issued credit Note to ABB and lodged refund claim of INR 14.41 Crores with GST authorities. The Company filed an Appeal on June 3, 2022 before Joint Commissioner of Commercial Taxes, Bengaluru and same was rejected on December 26, 2023 and September 24, 2024. Awaiting the formation of Goods and Service Tax Tribunal for filing appeals against the Joint Commissioner of Commercial Taxes (Appeals) order.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Assistant Commissioner of Commercial Taxes, Bengaluru
tax_litigation.status: The Company has filed appeals before the GST Appellate Tribunal on May 23, 2026 and May 25, 2026.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: In respect of Q2 FY 2022-23, refund claim of INR 19.39 Crores has been rejected by Deputy Commissioner of Commercial Taxes, Vadodara. Awaiting the formation of Goods and Service Tax Tribunal for filing appeal against the order.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has received an order from Assistant Commissioner (State Tax), Nandambakkam Assessment Circle, Chennai, Tamil Nadu (“GST Authority”) based on GST Assessment for the FY 2020- 21 with the demand of Penalty of Rs. 74,91,593/- under applicable provisions of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, the Integrated Goods & Services Tax Act, 2017, the Tamil Nadu Goods & Services Tax Act, 2017 and rules made thereunder. There is a total demand of INR 13.45 Crores (GST – INR 7.49 Crore plus interest & penalty – INR 5.96 Crores). The Company has received the order from the aforesaid authorities for alleged excess availment of Input Tax Credit (ITC) in GSTR-3B returns. Based on assessment of facts and prevailing law, the Company is of the view that the penalty levied is, arbitrary, unjustified and unsustainable in law. Accordingly, the Company has filed an appeal before Deputy Commissioner of State Taxes, Chennai on May 27, 2025 against the order passed by Assistant Commissioner of GST, Nandanam, Chennai. Pursuant to the appeal filed by the Company before the Deputy Commissioner of State Taxes, Chennai on May 27, 2025, against the assessment order issued by the Assistant Commissioner of GST, Nandanam, Chennai, a personal hearing was conducted on December 31, 2025. Pursuant to the hearing, Order-in-Appeal was passed on February 02, 2026 by the Deputy Commissioner (Appeals), Chennai, partially allowing the Company’s appeal and reducing the total demand from INR 13.45 Crores to INR 3.21 Crores (comprising GST of INR 1.69 Crores, interest of INR 1.35 Crores and penalty of INR 16.98 Lakhs). For the balance portion of the demand that has been disallowed, the Company proposes to file an appeal before the GST Appellate Tribunal, Chennai, once the Tribunal is constituted.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Assistant Commissioner of GST, Nandanam, Chennai
tax_litigation.status: The Company has filed an appeal before the GST Appellate Tribunal on June 30, 2026 for the balance demand.

tax_litigation.status: The Company has received an Order-in-Original from the GST authorities in Telangana for FY 2022-23 concerning the alleged excess availment of Input Tax Credit based on the reconciliation between GSTR-3B and GSTR-2A. The order has confirmed an IGST demand of INR 8.21 lakhs and Penalty of INR 0.82 lakhs The Company will file necessary appeal before the Appellate Authority along with necessary reconciliations in this regard within the permissible timeline. Based on assessment of facts and prevailing law, the Company is of the view that the Tax Demand and Penalty levied is arbitrary, unjustified and unsustainable in law.

operating_notes.text: HVDC revenue was about ₹1,100 Cr, roughly 15% of FY26 revenue of ₹8,147.7 Cr.
Exports are around 25-30% of revenue and orders excluding large HVDC orders, per management.
India's data centre capacity is under 2 GW, projected at 13-18 GW, and every data centre is 15% of addressable capex for Hitachi Energy.
Exports are about 25% of revenue and trending 25-26% of orders, per the CFO and CEO.
The 2 GW Tenet-linked European transmission package (three links delivering 6 GW) is worth around ₹1,700 Cr, part of the ₹5,096.5 Cr Q1FY27 intake.
About 60-65% of orders are pass-through on commodity, so commodity volatility had no material impact in Q1FY27.

timeline.summary: Hitachi Energy India reported QIP proceeds utilization of ₹469.66 Cr as of March 31, 2026.

Hitachi Energy India Limited’s Board of Directors will approve FY2026 audited results and dividend recommendation on **May 25, 2026**, per **Poovanna Ammatanda, General Counsel and Company Secretary**.
Hitachi Energy India Limited uploaded the audio recording of its May 26, 2026, 12:00–13:00 IST conference call with analysts/investors on its website.

Hitachi Energy India's May 26, 2026 Q4FY26 call disclosed a board-approved additional ₹2,000 Cr capex, including a greenfield large power transformer plant at Karjan, Vadodara, to produce transformers by Q4 CY2028, taking cumulative capex to about ₹4,000 Cr.
Hitachi Energy India filed its investor presentation for the ICICI Securities India Investor Conference.

On its 7 August 2026 Q1FY27 call, Hitachi Energy India reported revenue of ₹2,493.7 Cr (up 68.6% YoY), operating EBITDA of ₹399.9 Cr including a ₹36.37 Cr unrealised forex loss, orders of ₹5,096.5 Cr and a backlog of ₹32,222.1 Cr, and said construction began in June 2026 on its 20th plant at Karjan, Vadodara, targeted for December 2028.

watchlist.text: Order backlog execution and margin sustainability
Order inflow growth vs revenue growth

watchlist.response: Venu said base orders had strong growth for the full year and that some capacity is being taken by the HVDC portfolio, but gave no figure.
watchlist.text: Non-HVDC domestic order inflow appeared to fall in FY26 versus FY25, with base orders looking weak.

watchlist.response: Ajay Singh gave only a 25-30% ballpark and Venu said exact numbers could not be shared.
watchlist.text: Exact export order intake and revenue figures were requested.

watchlist.response: CFO attributed it to product mix and pointed to a 200 bps full-year improvement to 40%.
watchlist.text: Gross margin contracted sharply on a sequential basis.

watchlist.target: intake growth at or above revenue growth
watchlist.text: Order intake excluding HVDC versus revenue growth

watchlist.response: CFO first said gross margin had improved versus the previous quarter; when pressed on YoY, he conceded a slight contraction due to product mix.
watchlist.text: Analyst pressed on a 350 bps YoY gross-margin contraction and whether it was mix or commodity pass-through.

watchlist.response: CFO declined to give a segment margin or revenue split, saying only that HVDC revenue ramps from the second and third year; CEO said there is 'some contribution'.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked twice for the revenue contribution of the two HVDC projects in Q1FY27.

watchlist.response: CEO declined: 'we do not give specifically how much is HVDC... you should please respect that.'
watchlist.text: Analyst asked what share of the ₹32,222.1 Cr backlog is non-HVDC and how much is data centre.

watchlist.response: CEO said it is difficult to state at this stage as the technology needs to mature and localisation is required.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for the margin profile of the new BESS business.

watchlist.response: CEO declined to share segment-wise quantum.
